# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 41 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 41 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_041_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 10 — Drive Out Grief, Put on Cheerfulness

**41:1** "Get rid of grief," he said, "because she is the sister of doubt and bitterness." "But how is she their sister, lord?" I asked. "Bitterness and doubt seem like different things to me." "You really don't get it, do you?" he said. "Can't you see that grief is the most destructive of all the spirits? It does more damage to God's servants than anything else — it wears out the Holy Spirit and, in a different way, also rescues it."

**41:2** "I honestly don't follow you, lord," I said. "I can't understand how it can both wear out and rescue the Holy Spirit." "Let me explain," he said. "There are people who have never seriously looked into truth or asked questions about God — they just accepted what they were told. Then they got tangled up in business, money-making, friendships with unbelievers, and a hundred other worldly concerns. Those kinds of people can't grasp spiritual teachings. These preoccupations have clouded their minds, warped them, and left them spiritually empty."

**41:3** "But those who genuinely fear God — who ask real questions about God and truth, and who keep their hearts directed toward the Lord — everything becomes clear to them. They understand everything they hear, because the fear of the Lord is alive in them. Where the Lord lives, there is deep understanding. Stay close to the Lord, and you will understand and perceive everything."

**41:4** "Now listen, you slow learner — here's how grief wears out the Holy Spirit. When a double-minded person tries to do something and fails because of their double-mindedness, grief comes into them. That grief distresses the Holy Spirit and exhausts it."

**41:5** "Or when bitterness settles into someone — bitterness over a business deal, over food, over some stupid thing someone said, over a friend, over money given or received, over any number of silly things like that — grief seeps into the heart of that bitter person. They become agitated, and the Holy Spirit inside them is grieved."

**41:6** "Or take anger — when someone gets angry and bitter about something, grief enters again and makes their heart heavy. All of this exhausts the Holy Spirit. But now here's how grief can actually save: when a sinner sees his sins clearly and repents, the grief that hits him then is the grief of salvation. That kind of grief — grief over sin — saves. So there are two griefs at work: the grief that saves and the grief that destroys."

**41:7** "So put on cheerfulness. It always finds favor with God and pleases him — live in it. A cheerful person does good things, thinks good thoughts, and has no use for grief. But a sad, gloomy person? They always do harm. First, because they're distressing the Holy Spirit, which was given to humanity as a gift of joy. Second, because distressing the Holy Spirit leads to lawless behavior — they stop praying properly and stop giving thanks to God. So the prayer of a gloomy person never reaches God's altar."

**41:8** "Why not?" I asked. "Because grief is sitting in their heart," he said. "Grief mixed into prayer blocks it from rising to the altar pure and unhindered. It's like wine mixed with vinegar — it no longer has the same pleasant taste. In the same way, grief mixed into the Holy Spirit damages its power to intercede. So clean out that evil grief from your life and you will truly live for God. And everyone who throws off grief and wraps themselves in cheerfulness will live for God."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the pastoral urgency of Hermas's teaching on grief and joy.*
